results.claim: `branch -d` judges an upstream-tracking branch against its upstream, so the contract unsets the upstream first.
results.note: plain -d refuses although the branch is contained in HEAD; --unset-upstream then -d succeeds

results.claim: The upstream is read with for-each-ref (a full-refname @{upstream} fails) and restored with --set-upstream-to.
results.note: the contract records `%(upstream)|%(upstream:short)` and restores with the short name

results.claim: `worktree remove` refuses dirty, untracked-only and locked worktrees but silently deletes ignored files.
results.note: ignored files are deleted with rc=0, so the contract must gate them itself

results.claim: `worktree prune` is repository-wide; `worktree remove <path>` on a missing directory touches one entry.
results.note: global prune orphans commits held only by a detached worktree; scoped remove does not

results.claim: --no-ff always records a merge; a conflict aborts cleanly; unrelated histories are refused, not merged.

observed.unrelated_message: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories

results.note: target that is an ancestor of main still gets a merge commit

results.claim: A merge overwrites an ignored local file silently; `switch --no-overwrite-ignore` refuses; status hides it.
results.note: 'clean' cannot see ignored files, so the contract compares source paths with ignored files itself

results.claim: A tag named like a branch wins a bare-name lookup, so the contract uses refs/heads/<name> and SHAs.
results.note: bare name resolves to the tag; refs/heads/feat resolves to the branch

results.claim: On case-insensitive filesystems a differently-cased name may resolve; the exact listing never lists it.
results.note: match <branch> against the exact for-each-ref listing; a rev-parse success proves nothing

results.claim: A branch mid-rebase shows as a detached worktree; its name lives in rebase-merge/head-name.
results.note: the worktree list shows no branch; only rebase-merge/head-name maps the rebase back to topic

results.claim: status.showUntrackedFiles=no hides untracked files from plain status; --untracked-files=all still shows them.
results.note: the contract always passes --untracked-files=all when it tests for a clean workspace

results.claim: `merge-tree --write-tree` predicts conflicts (rc 1) and leaves refs, index and worktree untouched.
results.note: needs Git >= 2.38; the preview treats it as best-effort prediction

results.claim: Porcelain reports detached, locked (with reason) and prunable (missing directory) entries.
results.note: a prunable entry still names its branch, so git still treats that branch as checked out

results.claim: A cherry-pick sequence paused after a resolved step leaves only sequencer/, which status-based checks miss.
results.note: the contract lists sequencer/ as an in-progress marker

results.claim: Edits to a skip-worktree file are invisible to status, and `worktree remove` deletes them with rc=0.
results.note: the contract adds an `ls-files -v` check to 'clean'

results.claim: A tag named like the target makes bare-name containment checks lie; full refnames do not.
results.note: every revision argument in the contract uses refs/heads/<name>

results.claim: Removing the worktree a process is standing in is platform dependent; record it so the contract refuses it.
